The outward mapping — the domain writes LOR, the file receives EQL

The rule, stated where it is being applied

The vocabulary of this product is the practitioner’s. The domain says LOR — every screen, every column heading, every report label — and a format that carries the same quantity under its own name has that name translated at the boundary rather than adopted. The format definitions state the inward half of it: ESdat writes EQL, and EQL never reaches a screen.

An export is the identical rule read at the other end of the same boundary. The domain writes LOR and the file receives EQL, and nothing about that puts a second word in front of a practitioner — the format’s vocabulary goes into the file and stops there. What matters is that the mapping is a recorded table with a basis on every row, never an implicit rename. A translation nobody can look at is indistinguishable from a mistake nobody has found.

This is not the file’s whole column list. It is every place the two vocabularies differ and every place one of them has nothing — which is the same scope the inward table has, for the same reason.

Three tiers, and they are the inward table’s own

  • ✓ Established — 13 rows. A source states the equivalence, and the export writes it.
  • ⊘ Refused — 4 rows. A plausible field exists and no source states the equivalence, so the export writes nothing rather than a guess.
  • ✕ No counterpart — 6 rows. The target vocabulary has nothing that means this, and the file cannot carry it at all.

A mapping that was not evidenced enough to trust on the way in is not evidenced enough to write on the way out. 13 of 23 rows land; 4 are refused on evidence the export declines to manufacture; 6 have nothing on the other side at all.

A tier is a claim about evidence, not about confidence. “Does a source state this equivalence” has an answer somebody can check; “how sure is the matcher” is the inward question, and it belongs to a profile rather than here.

The outward mapping applied by this export — 23 rows, each with the basis it rests on.
The domain saysThe file receivesTierOn what basis
Limit of reporting (LOR)EQL✓ EstablishedThe inbound mapping ADR-0009 records, read outward. ESdat’s EQL becomes LOR on the way in; LOR becomes EQL on the way out, and neither direction is silent.
Method detection limit (MDL)MDL✓ EstablishedSame name, same meaning, in both directions.
AnalyteChemCode + OriginalChemName✓ EstablishedThe spec names the analyte across two fields — ChemCode is the key (“eg. CAS number”) and OriginalChemName the name — so the export writes the dictionary’s canonical name into OriginalChemName and its CAS-keyed code into ChemCode, never a synonym it happened to arrive under. The first draft of this row wrote “ChemName”, a field the Chemistry file does not have (W10-A-1).
Result valueResult✓ EstablishedWritten as reported. A non-detect keeps the laboratory’s own censoring notation rather than becoming a substituted number.
UnitResult_Unit✓ EstablishedThe spec’s unit column, distinct from Detection_Limit_Units — the two units the file keeps apart stay apart. The canonical unit is written, with any conversion this instance applied recorded in lineage here — the file carries the number and the unit, not the conversion. The first draft of this row wrote “Units”, a name the thirty published columns do not include (W10-A-1).
SampleSampleCode✓ EstablishedThe sample identifier as collected, which is the identifier the chain of custody and the certificate both name.
Fraction — dissolvedTotal_or_Filtered✓ EstablishedThe glossary’s Fraction entry states this mapping. Dissolved is what the number means; filtered is what was done, and the format’s word is the second one.
Sample type — primaryNormal✓ EstablishedELDF §5.
Sample type — trip blankTrip_B✓ EstablishedELDF §5. Trip_S appears in the spec’s prose and not in its code list, so the export writes the code list’s value.
Sample type — laboratory duplicateLAB_D✓ EstablishedELDF §5, which cases it both LAB_D and Lab_D; the export writes one and says which.
Sample type — matrix spikeMS✓ EstablishedELDF §5. It is a sample type and never a result type, and the export does not put it in the other column.
Sample type — matrix spike duplicateMS_D✓ EstablishedELDF §5.
Validation statenothing⊘ RefusedNo published field carries it — the Chemistry file’s thirty columns and the Sample file’s twelve include no validation state, and writing this instance’s own column name into somebody else’s file would invent a field. The state stays on the record; the transmittal can say it, the file cannot. The first draft of this row claimed the column existed (W10-A-1).
Qualifier — laboratory schemethe code, unchanged✓ EstablishedA U in an ESdat deliverable is USEPA’s U and means what USEPA says it means. The code belongs to its scheme, so it crosses without translation.
Practical quantitation limit (PQL)nothing⊘ RefusedRDL is the candidate field and no source states the equivalence. The importer refuses to fill PQL from RDL on the strength of the names; the export refuses the same trade in the other direction.
Qualifier — Strataflow schemenothing⊘ RefusedA reason code raised by one of this instance’s own checks is ours. Writing it into a laboratory qualifier field would export it as though a laboratory had said it, which the glossary forbids by name.
— (no domain term for the format’s ODL)left empty⊘ RefusedThe format carries a fourth limit no practitioner says. On the way in it must not be dropped; on the way out there is nothing to put in it, and the column is written empty rather than filled from a neighbour.
Sample type — field duplicateno code exists✕ No counterpartELDF has no field-duplicate code, though it does carry the pairing: Parent_Sample links a QC sample to its parent, and the export writes it. What cannot cross is the kind — a Normal row with a filled Parent_Sample is a parented sample of undefined type, so the RPD pairing’s meaning is lost while its link survives.
Sample type — field blankno code exists✕ No counterpartNo code found in the published code list.
Sample type — equipment blankno code exists✕ No counterpartNo code found in the published code list.
Exceedance outcomeno column exists✕ No counterpartAn EDD is a laboratory deliverable: it carries what was measured, not what was decided about it. An outcome is a result and a criterion together, and the criteria set does not cross in this file.
Qualifier propagation basisno column exists✕ No counterpartThe code travels; why it travelled does not. A rule firing and a hydrogeologist deciding produce the same letter, and only one of them survives a challenge.
Field dispositionno column exists✕ No counterpartA deliverable has a row per sample. A bore that was visited, dipped and found dry produced no sample, so it produces no row — and the file cannot say which kind of absence that is.

The reconciliation — the import’s proof, read at the other end

A migration proves what arrived. An export owes the mirror: a file leaving here is somebody else’s source and is trusted on the same evidence. Every row below says what it was counted over, because the round’s manifest and the results grid are two different populations of the same round and a proof that does not say which one it used is an assertion with a number on it.

10 checks. 5 agree; 5 cannot, and each of those names what it could not carry.
CheckCounted overIn the recordIn the fileVerdictWhat that means
Location rowsthe round’s manifest66●agreesThe 6 locations a sample in this round refers to, each written once.
Sample rowsthe round’s manifest1111●agrees6 primary and 5 field QC samples. Every one is written; 4 of them arrive without a type, which is the QC-code row below.
Result rowsthe round’s manifest155155●agreesEvery test on every sample on the manifest, including the controls.
Analytes on the results gridthe results grid1111●agreesThe dictionary’s canonical name for each, not the synonym the deliverable arrived under.
Non-detects, censoring notation keptthe results grid1414●agreesEach keeps the laboratory’s own “less-than” notation beside its reporting limit. None becomes a substituted number.
Locations in the round’s planthe grid’s columns76◐not carriedMW11 was visited and found dry, so it has no sample and therefore no row. The file cannot say that; its absence reads as data not yet sent.
Evaluation outcomesthe grid, 2 criteria sets1320◐no column66 results × 2 sets. The receiving system re-evaluates against its own criteria library, and a different criterion is a different answer.
— of those, indeterminatethe grid110■reads as a passA reporting limit above the criterion means nothing was measured either way. The file carries no state for it, and the incumbent baseline records one of the two incumbents rendering exactly this case as a pass unless a non-default setting is enabled — so these arrive as the one thing they are not.
QC samples carrying a type codethe round’s manifest51◐no code existsThe one trip blank has a published code. The two field duplicates (blind), one field blank, one equipment blank (rinsate) do not — and those are the controls that answer whether the sampling itself introduced anything.
Qualified results carrying their basisthe round’s QA/QC register100◐no columnJ and T on 10 results, each with the rule or the judgement it travelled on. The letter can cross; the basis cannot — and which of the letters may cross turns on a scheme these rows do not record.

5 of 10 rows agree, and the asymmetry with the import’s proof is the finding rather than a shortfall in the drawing.

The migration’s reconciliation can say agrees on every row it computes, because a file that arrived either matched its source or did not. This one cannot, and no amount of care would make it: 5 of the checks are about things the target vocabulary has no place for. An import can be complete; an export into somebody else’s format can only be honest about what it dropped. That is what makes the list below part of the proof rather than a caveat under it.

What the file cannot carry, named

A loss that is stated is a decision somebody can take — cover it in the transmittal, renegotiate the format, or accept it knowingly. A loss that is not stated is discovered by the person on the other end, months later, as a disagreement about what the data said. Each entry below carries what was checked before the claim was made, because “the format cannot carry it” is easy to write and easy to be wrong about.

The outcome against a criterion132 outcomes

Verified against what the format could carry: Both incumbents do emit an action-level code of their own, so the claim is not that a code cannot exist in the target. It is narrower and it holds: an outcome is a result and a criterion together, and this file carries no criteria set. A code written against the receiving library is that library’s answer, not this one’s.

What the receiving system reads instead: The receiving system evaluates the numbers against whatever it holds. Where its criteria are ours the answers agree by coincidence rather than by transfer; where they differ, nothing in the file says so.

Where it lives here — the results grid
Indeterminate — a reporting limit above the criterion11 outcomes

Verified against what the format could carry: Evaluation has four outcomes here and the formats this instance reads carry two. The absence is a missing state rather than a missing column, so no setting on the receiving side can recover it — there is nothing in the file to read. What the incumbent baseline records is the consequence measured on one of the two incumbents: it renders exactly this case as a pass unless a non-default setting is enabled.

What the receiving system reads instead: 11 results that are explicitly not passes arrive as a number, a reporting limit and no state — which any system comparing the two reads as compliant. It is the sharpest loss on the list, because the reader of the file is not told that anything was lost.

Where it lives here — the register of what could not be assessed
The field disposition — dry is not missing11 cells at MW11

Verified against what the format could carry: The location file could in principle carry a status column, and no source states one; more decisively, a deliverable has a row per sample, and a dry bore produced none. So the loss is structural rather than a field somebody forgot.

What the receiving system reads instead: MW11 is simply absent. A bore visited twice, dipped to the base of its screened interval and found dry is indistinguishable in this file from a bore whose results have not been sent — and those are different facts about the aquifer and about the round.

Where it lives here — the bore session that recorded it
The QC sample types the code list has no code for4 of 5 field QC samples

Verified against what the format could carry: Six of the nine sample types this domain uses map to a published code and three do not — and the Sample file does carry Parent_Sample, which links a QC sample to its parent, so the export writes the pairing. The three unmapped ones are exactly the field controls, which is not an accident: a laboratory receives a blind duplicate as an ordinary sample and never knew it was one.

What the receiving system reads instead: A field duplicate crosses as Normal with its Parent_Sample filled — a parented sample of undefined kind, so the RPD pairing’s meaning is lost while its link survives — and the two blanks have no code at all. The controls that answer “did the sampling introduce this” do not survive the crossing as what they are.

Where it lives here — the round’s manifest
The basis a qualifier travelled on10 qualified results

Verified against what the format could carry: A code belonging to a laboratory’s own vocabulary can cross intact, because the target reads that vocabulary. What has no field is the answer to “why did it reach these results”, which this instance requires on every propagated qualifier and which no published field carries.

What the receiving system reads instead: The letter, with nothing behind it. A rule firing under a named version and a hydrogeologist’s judgement produce the same character in the same column, and 10 further results carry a proposed qualifier that nothing has written — correctly, since no basis has been chosen.

Where it lives here — where every qualifier states its basis
A practical quantitation limit1 of the three limits this domain keeps apart

Verified against what the format could carry: A refusal rather than an absence, and the only one of the 4 refused mappings that costs a number. RDL is the plausible field and the equivalence is unverified; writing it would make the export assert something the importer declined to assert, on the very same evidence.

What the receiving system reads instead: Nothing, in that column. The receiving system sees two limits where this instance holds three, and the third is missing on purpose rather than by oversight.

Where it lives here — where the three limits are three columns

Dry is not missing, and this is where the distinction is lost

MW11 was visited twice on this round, dipped to the base of its screened interval and found dry. The results grid draws its column rather than removing it, and each of its 11 cells carries the disposition’s own glyph ○ and its own word: an absence of material, not a result below a limit of reporting, and not a pass.

None of that crosses. A deliverable has a row per sample; a bore that yielded no sample produces no row; so the file contains 6 locations where the round planned 7, and MW11 is simply not in it. A reader of the file cannot tell a dry bore from a bore whose results have not been sent yet — and those are different facts, one about the aquifer and one about the round.

This instance keeps the two apart on every surface it owns. The export is where the distinction meets a format that has never had it, and the honest thing to do is say so before the file is written rather than after somebody reads it.

The bore session that recorded itThe four states, everywhere

What the export does about it, which is not nothing

Every loss above is surfaced before the file is written, as a decision with named consequences rather than a warning to click past. Ambiguity is a decision the user makes, never a silent default — the same rule the exception queue keeps on the way in.

The three ways out, and the product does not choose between them.

  • Write, and cover it in the transmittal. The file as reconciled, plus this loss statement as the transmittal note the recipient reads first. The cost: Nothing, if the note is read. The record shows what was said, to whom, and when.
  • Write, and hold the affected rows. The 4 untyped QC samples held back rather than written as something they are not. The cost: A thinner file. A recipient computing precision from field duplicates gets no pairs at all rather than wrong ones.
  • Renegotiate the format. Nothing yet. The clause specifies a format that cannot carry this project’s QA/QC design, and the counterparty is told so. The cost: Time, and a conversation. It is the only option that fixes the cause rather than the symptom.

There is no fourth option where the file quietly writes a field duplicate as an ordinary sample and nobody is told. That is the option this screen exists to remove.

Where the send button would be

There is no send button on this recordand its absence is a decision

An export is a file and a manifest. It is written where the operator asked for it to be written, inside the customer’s own tenancy, and this instance holds no destination for it — no address, no endpoint, no queue.

The alerting precedent is one screen over and it is stricter than it looks: every alert destination is a configured row, a channel is the only place a dispatch can reach, and there is no relay behind it. An export has not even that, because an export is not dispatched at all.

The regulator returns this project already lodges work the same way and always have: the DWER portal, by hand, with the portal’s receipt kept as the evidence. What the product records is that a lodgement happened, not that it performed one.

Any integration that would route this data through vendor infrastructure is an anti-pattern to be redesigned rather than a feature to be configured. So the control below hands you a file; what happens to it afterwards is the contract’s business and yours.

Every destination is a configured rowDWER portal · manual lodgement

The two controls this record has, and the one it does not

  • Prepare an export. Runs the mapping, the reconciliation and the loss statement, and shows all three before anything is written. Where the data ends up: Nowhere. Nothing has been written yet.
  • Write the file set. Writes the 4 files and a manifest naming every count above, into the location the operator configured. Where the data ends up: The customer’s own tenancy, where it already was.
  • Send to… Does not exist. There is no destination field on this record, no endpoint to configure, and no relay behind one. Where the data ends up: nowhere — there is nothing here that moves it.

Alerting is the nearest thing this product has to sending, and it is stricter than it looks: a destination is a configured row in the customer’s own infrastructure, it is the only place a dispatch can reach, and a redirect is refused rather than followed. An export is a step further out again — it is not dispatched at all.

Read the absence as load-bearing rather than unfinished. A control that offered to deliver this file would need somewhere to deliver it from, and there is deliberately no such place.

One thing the export needs that this record does not hold

Found while drawing this — 2 September 2026deferred, owner unassigned

The qualifier scheme — the vocabulary a code belongs to — decides whether that code may be written into the file at all, and the QA/QC register does not carry one. A Strataflow reason code is this instance’s own. Exporting it as though a laboratory had said it is forbidden by name, so the scheme is what the export would filter on.

Four codes are affected on this round: J and T are applied to 10 results between them, and L and B are proposed and unapplied. Which of the four belongs to a laboratory’s vocabulary and which to this instance’s is exactly the question the export has to answer, and the register answers a different one — it records the basis each qualifier travelled on, which is what an auditor asks and not what a file writer needs.

The QA/QC register carries each qualifier’s propagation basis and not its scheme. Adding one means deciding the vocabulary of four codes, on screens that already draw them — which is a decision rather than a column. It is recorded here rather than closed in passing, because guessing the vocabulary of a code is the same mistake as guessing a field mapping — and the whole of this screen is about not doing that.

Where every qualifier states its basisThe decision layer

What this screen deliberately does not do

It does not draw a format zoo. Parity with the incumbent across its full domain breadth is a stated non-goal, and drawing ten outbound formats would perform coverage rather than earn it. One export is drawn all the way down instead: the mapping with a basis on every row, the reconciliation with a population named on every check, and the losses with what was verified beside each one.

It does not invent field names. Every landed row of the mapping table rests on a mapping this project already recorded on the way in. Where the evidence stops, the table stops — 4 rows write nothing on purpose — rather than continuing with plausible-looking columns nobody can cite.

It does not upgrade the data on the way past. The round leaves at the validation state it is in. An export that quietly wrote a better state than the record holds would be the one failure mode worse than losing a column.

Field capture — 2026-Q2-GW

One bore at a time, in the order the work happens — with the round grid as the summary over them.

a proposal — not in the product

Proposed — and redesigned rather than deepened. Nothing in FR-1 to FR-8 covers field data capture.

U1 is named the highest-frequency user, and every requirement in the PRD is about what happens after a laboratory has already reported. The water level, the purge volume, the field pH and the observation that a bore was dry are still collected by hand and typed in later, or lost. What changed is the axis: the first drawing entered a round column by column across bores, and a senior hydrogeologist read it and said that is not how the work runs — “I don’t measure the SWL at seven bores, then return conceptually to MW05 to enter its pH.” The grid below is now the summary, and the session under it is the screen.

That is the arithmetic working, not failing: a sample on the manifest that no session claims is either a control with no bore or a visit somebody forgot to record, and the two are told apart by which it is.

The seven dispositions, and why “dry” is one of them

A closed list. Every state but the first requires a reason, and the last one is the residual.
StateReasonThis roundWhat it means
●Samplednot required6 nowWater was recovered and one or more samples were submitted under the chain of custody.
○Dry◐required1 nowThe bore was reached and dipped and held no water. A measurement of the aquifer, not a gap in the record — the hydrograph draws a break rather than a line through it and the round is satisfied as attempted.
◔Insufficient recharge◐required0The bore held water, was purged dry, and did not recover enough to fill the containers before the crew had to leave.
⊘Inaccessible◐required0 now · 1 across visitsThe bore could not be reached — a cut track, a locked gate, stock, fire, or a working area closed to entry.
▲Damaged or obstructed◐required0The headworks or the casing prevented the visit: a sheared riser, a seized cap, an obstruction above the screen.
?Not located◐required0The crew searched the surveyed position and did not find the bore. It is a finding about the register, and it routes to the location record rather than to the round.
—Not sampled◐required0The residual state, and the reason is free text because the six above did not fit. A round left with this disposition and no reason cannot be marked complete.

A dry bore is not a missing reading. The hydrograph draws a break rather than a line through it, the sampling programme reads the round as attempted rather than uncollected, and the report says so. Left as an absence all three go wrong quietly, and the register cannot tell a bore nobody visited from a bore with no water in it.

The vocabulary is exercised rather than declared: this round used 3 of the seven. MW11 was inaccessible on 2026-05-13 — the creek crossing was running — and dry when the crew got back to it on 2026-05-14. Two visits in one round are two records, not one overwriting the other.

Captured is not synced, and the board can tell

3 records sit on Field tablet WDL-FT-02 and not on the record, holding 8 mandatory fields between them.

That is why the obligation board and the programme still read this round overdue by 10 days at MW11 — 2026-05-14 to 2026-05-24, counted rather than typed. A countdown reads the record, and the record does not know what the crew knows.

The capture timestamp is kept, not the sync timestamp

Offline by design: the site has no signal. Records are captured locally, queued, and written when the vehicle reaches the gate — and the record keeps the time the crew stood at the bore, because a round that reads as though every bore was visited at 18:41 from the highway is a round nobody can defend.

A parameter is holding when the spread across the three readings — the largest minus the smallest — sits inside its tolerance, measured against their mean where the tolerance is a percentage. The looser reading of “± 3%”, each reading within 3% of the mean, allows twice the movement, and which one is meant decides whether a bore stabilised — so it is stated rather than assumed. Turbidity is the one disjunctive rule: below 10 NTU a reading is acceptable outright, and only above that does the ± 10% agreement test apply. A falling turbidity curve never satisfies a percentage test on its way down, and a conjunctive reading would fail every low-flow sample ever taken.

Before the round can be marked complete

The preflight the review asked for. It is not a checklist somebody ticks: every count is derived from the 8 sessions above, so a round with a bore outstanding cannot read as ready however carefully the list was filled in.

Every line counted off the sessions above. Nothing here is asserted.

The round cannot be marked complete yet — 2 things hold it.

3 records are on Field tablet WDL-FT-02 and not on the record; and 1 instrument has no post-round check. The control below states what it would write and stays refusable rather than silently disabled: a greyed-out button that will not say why is how a field officer at a gate loses an afternoon.

Marking 2026-Q2-GW complete — what that writes, before you press it:

  • Sampling round marked satisfied on the programme1 — naming the sampling event that satisfied it
  • Locations whose disposition becomes the round’s answer7
  • Dry locations recorded as attempted rather than missed1 — waived with the reason on it, never deleted
  • Obligation countdowns that stop1 — the quarterly groundwater round
  • Records that would still be on the device afterwards3 — and this is what holds it

Reversible while the round is open: completion is a state on the round, recorded with who set it and when, and it can be reopened with a reason. What cannot be undone is the sync — a captured record, once written, is superseded rather than replaced.

One-handed, at a bore, on a phone

375 px is the primary layout for this screen and the desktop is the secondary one, which is the opposite of every other screen in this catalogue. A field officer is standing at a headworks in the sun with a tablet in one hand and a dipper in the other.

So the session stacks rather than pans: every step is full width, every control clears 44 px under a coarse pointer, and the sequence runs vertically because a thumb scrolls down. The stabilisation series is the one thing that pans, with its time column frozen — nine columns cannot stack without losing the comparison between consecutive readings, which is the only thing the series is for.

The keyboard contract moved with the axis. Tab walks down the session, Enter adds a reading to the open series, and D is gone: a single key that marked a bore dry was right when dry was the only alternative to sampled, and it is wrong now there are six.

What this screen does not own

Purge and stabilisation is the same series read in full, with the tolerances, the field-against-laboratory conductivity check and the bore that never stabilised. A deeper view of these rows, not a second copy of them.

Chain of custody owns the containers once they leave the bore — the transfers, the seals, and the disagreement about one seal number. The session creates the chain; it does not hold it.

Sampling events owns the round as a record: the manifest, the QC taxonomy and what the laboratory received. The programme owns what was owed, and when.

What the round was held to, what followed automatically, and what is still yours to decide.

3NEED DECISION

3 findings stand between this round and validation, and each one needs a hydrogeologist rather than a rule.

Matrix spike recovery — PAS-WO-268841 · zinc · Equipment blank — WDL-26Q2-QC3 · bladder pump, after MW05 · Spike against history — Electrical conductivity · MW05. Between them they hold 11 results whose qualifiers have been proposed and not applied. Advance to validated is refused until they are settled, and it says so rather than being greyed out with no reason: a control that will not explain itself is a control people learn to work around.

The workflow, and where the round sits on it

1. Unresolved3A finding nobody has looked at, or has looked at and not decided. The round cannot leave this state on its own.
2. Reviewed1Somebody has read it and recorded what they found, and the disposition is waiting on something outside this screen.
3. Dispositioned5Settled — by a deterministic rule that names itself, or by a person who names themselves. Both are on the record and they are told apart.
4. Ready for validation10The check passed and nothing followed. It is not a decision that was made; it is a decision that was never owed.

The round moves right only when the first column empties. This is a different axis from the validation state — imported → screened → validated → approved → published runs over results, and this one runs over findings. Conflating them is how a round advances with three open questions on it: the results were all screened, so the button looked ready.

The 3 findings that are yours

Need decision

Matrix spike recovery — PAS-WO-268841 · zinc

failQC outcome

Zinc recovered 62% in this water and reproduced at 64%. Which zinc results does that reach, and on whose authority?

Zinc recovered 62% against a 70–130% limit, reproduced at 64% on the spike duplicate. Matrix interference, not a one-off.

Nine results are in the batch and one of them is the MW05 exceedance at 31.6 µg/L. A recovery below 100% biases low, so a qualified exceedance is understated rather than doubtful — but the qualifier is an assertion about eight samples nobody spiked, and an auditor five years from now will ask who made it.

Every way out, what it writes, and whether it is available on this evidence.

The laboratory’s qualifier applies batch-wide◈Laboratory qualifier — applies batch-wideQualifier L on 9 results, origin laboratory, attributed to Pilbara Analytical Services.■not on this evidenceNot available on this certificate. PAS-WO-268841 reports the spike recovery on its QC page and carries no result-level qualifier, so taking this option would attribute to the laboratory something it did not say.
A project data quality objective rule applies§Project data quality objective ruleQualifier L on every zinc result in the batch, origin rule, with DQO 2025.2 named on each.■not on this evidenceNot available under 2025.2. Its matrix spike rule states the 70–130% limit and no propagation action, and a rule that says nothing cannot be cited as having said this. Adding the action is a new DQO version, and that is where it belongs.
A hydrogeologist’s disposition — batch-wide✍A hydrogeologist’s dispositionQualifier L on 9 results, origin manual, naming you, the date, and the reason you give. Every result carries “dispositioned by” rather than a rule reference.●availableThe honest basis for this case: the interference is reproducible across the spike duplicate, the batch is one water type from one round, and extending it is a professional judgement somebody has to own.
Sample-specific only·Sample-specific onlyQualifier L on 1 result — zinc in WDL-26Q2-005, the sample the spike was made from. The other eight carry nothing.●availableDefensible and narrow: a spike measures recovery in the aliquot it was added to. It leaves the MW05 exceedance unqualified, which is the consequence to weigh.

Refused: Apply it silently because the spike failed. That is the inference the review named — a propagated qualifier with no basis on it is indistinguishable from one somebody decided, and only one of those survives a challenge.

Whichever is taken is written with your name, the time and your reason on it, and the finding moves to Dispositioned. A manual qualifier carries who applied it and why; a laboratory one carries neither, because the laboratory said it and the import records who loaded the file.

3410 µS/cm against a prior-round median of 2120 µS/cm at this bore — a modified z-score of 6.2 on 11 rounds of its own record, against a 3.5 threshold.

Whichever is taken is written with your name, the time and your reason on it, and the finding moves to Dispositioned. A manual qualifier carries who applied it and why; a laboratory one carries neither, because the laboratory said it and the import records who loaded the file.

Every check, and which of the three things it is

Three concepts were mixed under one word: the QC outcome, the automatic consequence, and the professional disposition.

A holding time exceeded quarantines a result and a reporting limit above a criterion records an indeterminate outcome — both deterministic, both named by the rule that did it. Equipment-blank contamination and a step in a bore’s own conductivity are not: they need somebody accountable. The column that used to say pass / warn / fail now says all three things, and the outcome is the one that says what the check did to the data.

Where every qualifier came from

A propagated qualifier states its basis, on every result it reached.

“Why did this qualifier propagate to these results?” is exactly the type of thing an auditor may ask five years later, and the answer is one of four: the laboratory said it in the deliverable · a project data quality objective rule applies · a named person dispositioned it · it is specific to the sample it was raised on. A qualifier with no basis on it cannot be told from an inference, and only one of those survives a challenge.

The one the review named — PAS-WO-268841 · zinc

The drawn version of this said “Qualifier L — biased low — on all 9 zinc results in the batch” and stopped. Read at speed that is a rule firing. It is not: PAS-WO-268841 reports the recovery on its QC page and qualifies no sample result, and DQO 2025.2’s matrix spike rule states the 70–130% limit and no consequence. So the propagation had no basis, and the honest basis is the third one — somebody has to decide it and own it.

Which direction the bias runs is the finding, and the decision does not change it: a recovery below 100% biases low, so a qualified exceedance is understated rather than doubtful. What the decision changes is how many results carry the caveat, and who said they should.

Re-running, and what it would be re-run against (2025.2 · 2026.1)

2025.2 was used for this round · 2026.1 is current. The findings above were raised on 2026-05-19 10:22 AWST under 2025.2, which was in force 2025-07-01 → 2026-05-20. 2026.1 took effect 2026-05-21 → — Two changes, both tightening: the field duplicate limit, and an explicit consequence on the equipment blank rule that 2025.2 stated no action for.

What the current version would change on this round, computed rather than promised.
Under 2025.2Under 2026.1
Checks whose outcome moves—0
Checks that stop needing a decision3 open1 becomes automatic
Results newly qualified by rule01
Findings already raised that are re-judged—0

Equipment blank — WDL-26Q2-QC3 · bladder pump, after MW05: Under 2026.1 this stops being a decision. The blank rule gains an explicit consequence — a detection above the limit of reporting qualifies every result for that analyte collected with the same equipment after the rinse — so MW07’s zinc would take qualifier B automatically, with the rule and its version as the basis instead of a person.

A re-run does not re-judge a finding already raised: it produces a second assessment under a second version and both stay readable, because every finding carries the rule version it was raised under. That is the same property a criteria set has, and it is why the button says which version rather than just “Re-run checks”. The objectives, both versions.

A reporting limit above the criterion is not a pass.

Cadmium was reported at <1.0 µg/L against an ANZG 2018 guideline value of 0.54 µg/L. Nothing was measured either way, so the outcome is indeterminate and it is drawn as its own mark. Recording that as compliance is the single most consequential error this product exists to prevent — and it is one of the four consequences above that follow automatically, because the comparison is arithmetic on two numbers and there is nothing in it for anybody to decide.

Spike against history — a finding with no limit behind it

Electrical conductivity at MW05 — 3410 µS/cm this round

Flagged against this bore’s own record, not against a fixed limit. Eleven rounds of rise and then a step: the trend explains part of this and not the size of it. The finding is raised, not resolved — whether it is a step change in the seepage plume or a sampling artefact is a question for the trend test and the purge record, and the product does not guess between them.

Laboratory batches

The unit QC is actually run on, and everything it qualifies.

/projects/:projectId/batches

A control sample applies to a batch, not to a sample.

Laboratories work in batches — a work order, prepared and analysed together — and one method blank, one control sample and one matrix spike cover all of them. Without the batch, “which results does this failed spike qualify?” has no answer, and a single failure either qualifies nothing or is applied to everything out of caution. Both are wrong.

Zinc matrix-spike recovery of 62% is below the 70% limit and it is reproducible across the duplicate, so this is matrix interference rather than a one-off. Every zinc result in this batch — nine samples, including the MW05 exceedance at 31.6 µg/L — is qualified as biased low. A recovery below 100% biasing low means the true value is likely higher, so the exceedance stands and is if anything understated.

Nothing qualified. The PFAS exceedance carries no batch caveat.

One thing on this screen does not reconcile, and it is recorded rather than left to be noticed

The PFAS batch YAR-B-118420 states 4 samples. The manifest gives the two PFAS tests to one sample, WDL-26Q2-003 — the only one carrying 16 tests and 5 containers. The grid carries a PFOS + PFHxS total at 6 locations. Three readings of how far one suite reached, and they are not the same number.

All three predate this wave, which met the disagreement while chaining the PFAS result to the records that produced it and did not settle it. Settling it means choosing, and the cheapest choice empties four cells of the crosstab’s PFAS row — the row the non-detect rule is demonstrated over. That is a decision with a drawn argument on the other end of it rather than a count to nudge.

What the lineage does instead is name this batch and link it. Nothing drawn this wave rests on which reading wins.

A recovery below 100% is not simply “bad data”

The zinc spike recovered 62% of what was added, reproducibly across the duplicate. That is matrix interference — something in this water suppresses the measurement — and it means the reported zinc is biased low.

Which direction the bias runs is the whole finding. A result already above the guideline value, biased low, exceeds by at least the factor shown. The exceedance is strengthened, not weakened, and a screen that reported only “QC failed” would have left a practitioner to argue the opposite.

Zinc · MW05

Reported 31.6 µg/L against a criterion of 8.0 µg/L — 4.0×. Corrected for 62% recovery the true value is nearer 51 µg/L, or 6.4×. The reported value is used; the correction is stated and never silently applied, because a recovery-corrected number is an estimate and the certificate is a measurement.

Data quality objectives

The acceptance limits every QC check is measured against, and where each one comes from.

/projects/:projectId/objectives

A guideline value gets a version, an effective date and a source. A QC limit is the same kind of object and was not treated as one.

A regulator asking “why 30%?” is asking exactly the question they ask about a criterion. Hard-coding the answer means the product cannot say, and means a customer whose own data quality objectives are tighter has no way to apply them without a release.

Two versions of one set. A limit is versioned with an effective span exactly as a criteria set is, and a finding carries the version it was raised under.

Two of the ten rules moved in 2026.1, and the second is the interesting one. The matrix spike rule states a limit and no consequence — which is why a failed spike on PAS-WO-268841 raises a finding that needs a hydrogeologist rather than a qualifier that applies itself. The blank rule had the same shape until 2026.1 gave it one, and that single addition is what moves one finding on the last round out of the decision queue. A rule that states a number and not what follows from it is a rule that hands every instance of itself to a person.

The applicability rule is the part that was wrong

Relative percent difference near the limit of reporting

RPD is only meaningful when both results sit well above the reporting limit. A duplicate pair of 1.2 and 1.8 µg/L against a 1.0 µg/L limit gives an RPD of 40% and means nothing at all — the two numbers are the same measurement inside its own uncertainty.

Applying the 30% limit to every pair raises a failure on almost every near-limit duplicate, and a QC flag that is usually noise is a QC flag people stop reading. Above 5 × LOR the percentage applies; below it, an absolute difference of 2 × LOR does.

Zinc at MW05: 21.4 and 31.6 µg/L, both above 5 × LOR — the 38.2% failure is real

Changing a limit reaches forward only

Field duplicate RPD moved from 25% to 30% on 2025-07-01, and the 5 × LOR applicability rule was added in the same revision. Results evaluated before that date keep the limits in force then.

And it happened again on 2026-05-21: Field duplicate RPD went from ≤ 30% to ≤ 25%, and Field / trip / equipment blank went from < LOR, with no stated consequence to < LOR — and a detection above it qualifies every result for that analyte collected with the same equipment after the rinse, in that event.

What 2026.1 did to the round already assessed under 2025.2 — computed on the QA/QC workspace, not promised here.
Count

Findings that stop needing a hydrogeologist1
Results a rule would newly qualify1
Reports already issued that change0

Tightening the field duplicate limit again — from ≤ 25% to ≤ 20% — would:

  • Future pairs newly failing, on last year’s data4
  • Historical QC outcomes rewritten0
  • Reports already issued that would change0
  • New version created1 — 2026.2, effective on a date you choose

A limit is versioned with an effective date, exactly as a criteria set is. A result evaluated under 2025.2 keeps that verdict, and the version that produced it is on the result.

Data quality assessment

3 objectives were not met, and 3 findings across the six dimensions have not been dispositioned — including one under a dimension whose verdict reads met.

A QA/QC table lists checks. An assessment says whether the data is fit for the purpose it was collected for — which is a judgement made against objectives written down beforehand, not a verdict assembled afterwards from whatever passed. And a verdict rests on findings, so each row below says how many of its findings were settled and by whom: a rule that named itself, or a person who did. A dimension carrying an open finding is provisional however confident its verdict reads.

The Settled by column is the one the practitioner review asked for. Where it names a rule and a version — Field duplicate RPD · DQO 2025.2 · ≤ 30% above 5 × LOR — the consequence was deterministic and nobody had to decide it. Where it names a person, somebody did, and their reason is on the finding. Where it says nobody yet, the dimension’s verdict is a statement about data whose qualifiers have not been applied.

What “not met” actually costs

Not metConsequence for the assessment
Sensitivity — cadmiumCadmium cannot be assessed at any location. Seven results are reported as unassessable rather than compliant, and the recommendation is a method change from Q3. Settled automatically: the reporting limit sits above the criterion and the comparison is arithmetic.
Accuracy — zincNine zinc results would be qualified biased low — and none of them is yet. The propagation basis is the open decision on PAS-WO-268841: the certificate carries no result-level qualifier and DQO 2025.2 states no consequence for the failed spike, so a hydrogeologist has to say how far it reaches. The MW05 exceedance stands and is understated either way; no result is corrected.
Completeness — 79%Below the 95% objective. MW11 yielded nothing — the crew reached it and found it dry, which is a measurement of the aquifer rather than a gap — and MW09 is a result short on a cracked container. The round is reported as incomplete rather than as a clean 63, and the dry bore is reported as attempted rather than missed.

Written before the round, not after it

The objectives on this page were set when the programme was designed. That ordering is the whole point: an assessment written after the results are in is an argument, and every practitioner who has read one knows the difference.

Where an objective was not met the product does not soften it, and does not quietly drop the dimension from the report. It states the shortfall, its consequence and the remedy — which is what makes the rest of the report credible.

Comparability — met

Arsenic’s reporting limit stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L in May 2025 on a method change. It is recorded, it is drawn as a stepped line on every plate that spans it, and the trend test treats the earlier censored values as censored rather than as measurements. A series whose limit changed silently mid-way is a trend nobody can defend.

MW05 — what the shortfall means

The cation–anion balance at MW05 is −0.04%, well inside the ± 5% limit. What fails is the reconciliation: the reported ions sum to 1,698 mg/L of dissolved solids and the laboratory reports 2,240 — a ratio of 1.32 against 0.90 – 1.10.

A charge balance can be perfect while a third of the mass is unaccounted for, and that is what it is saying here: the charges match because the suite is internally coherent, and 542 mg/L of it was never reported. On a bore whose sulfate is 917 mg/L, the likely readings are an unreported constituent — silica, an organic load, or a cation the suite does not include.

It is raised as a review item rather than resolved. The product does not know which, and guessing would be a silent derivation (PP3).

How each number here is made

Two reported values per bore. Everything else on this screen is arithmetic over the ion table.

Total vs dissolvedNot run. This round’s metals suite is USEPA 200.8 — dissolved metals — there is no total result to compare a dissolved one against, and a check reported as passing on a pair that does not exist is worse than one reported as not run.no pair

MW05’s conductivity is not typed here either: it is the last round of the bore’s own record, the same 3,410 µS/cm the licence condition is assessed against.

The rider that landed here, and what it moved

Until 2 September 2026 the five balances on this screen were typed strings sitting beside the ion table that refutes them. Recomputed, every one of them moved, and the largest move was the one the argument rested on.

The review item at MW05 survives and is now on the check that can see it. That is the useful half of the finding: the typed number and the derived one both said look at this bore, and only one of them could say why.

Recorded rather than quietly repaired, because a catalogue whose method is derived counts should be able to show what a typed one cost. Wave 7 found this and wrote it down; wave 8 paid it.

▲ marks a round above the criterion and · one below it, so the run reads across the row without reading the numbers.

Twelve series are evaluated — three parameters at four bores. Eight have no round above the criterion anywhere in the window and are not drawn; a register of nothing happening is not a finding, and it would bury the four that are.

What each outcome did, in words

○not triggered Zinc (filtered) at MW07. The first round above the criterion at this bore. Two more consecutive rounds would oblige a notification; one round below resets the count to nothing.

The equipment blank taken after the pump was used at MW05 carries 1.4 µg/L of zinc, so carry-over cannot be ruled out on this result — a run that begins on a qualified result is worth watching rather than acting on.

◐one round short Zinc (filtered) at MW05. One round short. A third consecutive exceedance in 2026 Q3 trips the condition, and the monthly programme now running at this bore means that round arrives in weeks rather than in a quarter.

■triggered Copper (filtered) at MW05 — tripped on 2026-Q1-GW. Tripped on 2026-Q1-GW, which is the round the 30-day clock ran from. This round extends the run and raises nothing new — the obligation is the one already lodged, and the response it obliged is the TARP Level 2 escalation in force since 2026-03-01.

◐one round short Electrical conductivity at MW05. One round short, on the licence limit rather than a guideline value. The same four numbers are the tail of the record the QA/QC outlier check measured this round’s value against — one series, two questions, and they do not have the same answer.

Why the outcome is stored rather than re-computed

The window and the criterion in force at each round are frozen onto the outcome. A licence varied next year re-evaluates future rounds and moves nothing already decided — the same rule the notification screen keeps about a deadline.

The site’s own TARP is a second window over the same rounds and it is stricter — Level 2 escalates on two consecutive rounds, not three, which is why monthly sampling at MW05 has been running since March while the licence condition has tripped once. The two windows are drawn apart on purpose: the licence is what a regulator enforces and the TARP is what the site committed to, and a product that merges them loses which one was breached.

If the window were widened to five rounds, before anybody widened it:

  • Series whose outcome would change0 — a longer window cannot break a run that is already unbroken
  • Outcomes already decided1 — copper at MW05, frozen with the rule that decided it
  • Obligations that would be re-raised0
  • Rounds that would be re-evaluated9 — every round in the new window, on the criterion in force at each

Reversible, and nothing is written by the preview. A condition change re-evaluates forward; outcomes already frozen onto an obligation stay as they were decided.

1–11 of 11 analytes

MW11 is drawn empty, and the column says why.

The field record for this round has MW11 visited twice and found dry — dipped to the base of the screened interval, tape dry to the weight — so it yielded no samples and there is nothing to put in these 11 cells. The column stays: a column that disappears reads as a bore that does not exist, and a cell left blank reads as a value somebody forgot to enter. Neither is what happened. The cells carry the round’s own dry disposition — its glyph and its word, read from the same list the bore session dispositions against, so the grid does not invent a second vocabulary for one fact — and the sentence a screen reader gets carries the whole of what dry means, and the 66 results counted above are the ones that exist. The bore session holds the disposition; Data states is where the pattern is set out.

The same grid, across rounds

One round is a snapshot. The comparison is the review.

Analyte by location answers what did we get. Analyte by round answers is it moving, which is the question a quarterly review exists to ask and the reason a saved view says “rolling four quarters”. The same marks, the same censoring notation, the same criteria sets — the axis changes and nothing else does.

MW05 · rolling four quarters. Two marks per value, always in the same order.

What only the second layout shows

Arsenic, zinc, sulfate and hardness are all rising together, quarter on quarter, at one bore. No single round says that — every one of them is just a number against a limit.

And the cadmium row shows something a single round hides completely: the reporting limit stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L between Q3 and Q4 when the laboratory changed method. The Q3 cell is indeterminate against both criteria sets; the later ones only against ANZG. A series that silently mixed two reporting limits would read as an improvement.

Rising hardness is not a background detail

Hardness went from 244 to 412 mg/L over the same four quarters, and cadmium, nickel and zinc are all assessed against criteria computed from it.

So the criteria moved too. The zinc criterion was 5.4 µg/L in 2025 Q3 and is 8.0 µg/L now — the limit relaxed while the result climbed, and the exceedance factor understates the change. Nothing on a single-round grid could tell you that.

How the criterion is calculatedAgainst background

The same grid, a different matrix

2026-M05-SOIL · collected 6–7 May 2026 · Pilbara Analytical Services certificate PAS2026-04361 · 5 analytes × 11 samples · 35 results · 20 cells at an increment that was composited before it was analysed

The axis changes, and the domain forces it: these columns are samples, not locations.

Two of them belong to four places each. A composite is collected across positions, so a grid drawn analyte × location has nowhere to put one — and drawing it at the place of its first increment would be a lie with a coordinate on it. Everything else is the same: the same marks, the same censoring notation, the same criteria sets in the same order. The four WDL-26M5-C02 increments are columns for the reason MW11 is a column above — material that was collected and produced no number is not the same thing as material nobody collected.

All 35 results read not evaluated, and that is computed rather than cautious.

Applicability is by matrix among other things, the criteria library holds 5 sets, and 0 of them carry a soil or sediment matrix — every one is freshwater or groundwater. So no criterion is selectable and nothing is asserted about any of these numbers. Not evaluated is not compliant and the marks keep them apart. Two roads reach this state and the product does not run them together: a sample whose matrix nobody stated arrives here because nothing could be chosen, and a sample whose matrix is stated and for which the library holds no set arrives here because of a configuration decision — which somebody can close, deliberately, with an effective date and a version. This investigation does not close it on its way past.

The 4 increment columns carry a glyph and a word rather than a blank, and they carry no outcome marks at all: nothing was measured, so nothing was assessed, and a not evaluated mark on them would assert a result that no criterion happened to fit. What they are is material that exists, in a jar, with the analysis unbought — and the composite record says until when.

What is said instead of an outcome

With nothing selectable, the comparison a practitioner makes is against the site’s own background — TP05, sampled on the same round by the same crew from the equivalent horizon. It is an interpretation, not an outcome: it gets no mark on the grid and it makes nothing an exceedance.

Ratio to WDL-26M5-S05 at TP05. A ratio is not a criterion.

pH is not ratioed. It is a logarithm, so “1.09 times background” would be a number about nothing. And WDL-26M5-D01 is not on this table: Sediment, and the investigation collected no upstream sediment control. A soil background is not one, so this sample has a number and no comparison — which is a finding about the design rather than about the creek.

The one number on the grid with no comparison at all

WDL-26M5-D01 is the sediment sample, collected at SW01 — a location whose class is surface water. The glossary’s matrix entry uses exactly this pairing as its example, and the consequence is on this grid: it has five results, no criterion, and no background of its own, because the investigation collected no upstream creek-bed control.

Dividing it by a soil background would be a comparison across matrices — the quiet one the glossary refuses. So the cell says nothing rather than something convenient, and the finding is about the sampling design rather than about the creek.

What would close it

One sediment sample upstream of the discharge point, on the next surface-water round. It is a line in a sampling plan, not a change to this product — and recording that it is missing is what makes it a line somebody writes.

The composites behind two of these columnsThe round that collected themWhy nothing applies

Everything true about a value is on the value.

A superseded reading keeps its old value struck through beside the new one. A quarantined reading stays visible in brackets on a hatched ground rather than vanishing. A non-detect keeps the laboratory’s own <LOR notation and is never rendered as a substituted number.

The column set is a saved view, not a rebuild

The monthly review is a recall. Which locations, which analytes, which period, which criteria sets — the whole question, named and shared, so two people asking for “the compliance boundary numbers” get the same rows.

Three limits, and they are not the same number.

The incumbents carry these separately too — this is parity, not a differentiator — and the bar is that they never collapse into one. An LOR is what the laboratory will report to; an MDL is what the method can distinguish from noise; a PQL is what it can quantify reliably. Evaluating against a criterion uses the LOR, and the other two stay on the record because a re-analysis argument is made from them.

The state that is not a pass

A non-detect at an LOR of 1.0 µg/L against a criterion of 0.54 µg/L means nothing was measured either way. The laboratory did not find cadmium above 1.0; the criterion sits below that; the result is silent about the criterion.

An incumbent renders this as compliant by default, and a documented support thread records exactly that happening — <0.60 against a 0.5 standard, flagged in the alert email and shown as a pass in the chemistry table until a non-default setting was enabled. Two surfaces of the same product disagreed, and the default was the wrong one.

Here it is its own state, identically on every surface that shows it: this page, the crosstab, the box plot, the summary table, the report and the Excel export.

The two chains part at the bench, and the divergence is the 2 hops this one does not take.

Everything above is shared: the same bore, the same session, the same purge, the same custody transfers, the same cooler at 4.2 °C. From the bench they separate — cadmium was determined in PAS-WO-268841 by USEPA 200.8 · ICP-MS, and the PFAS fraction left on a subcontract to another laboratory under its own custody record. That divergence is why a batch-level qualifier reaches one and not the other, and it is the thing a chain drawn per-certificate rather than per-sample cannot show.

How this criterion was calculated

A hardness-modified guideline value, and every input that produced it.

/projects/:projectId/hardness

A criterion that is a function of another result inherits everything true about that result.

Cadmium, nickel and zinc at this site are assessed against values computed from hardness. If the hardness is wrong — wrong sample, wrong date, derived rather than measured, or above the range the relationship is defined over — then three exceedances are wrong with it, and nothing on a conventional results screen would show you that.

The hardness this criterion used

Sample
WDL-26Q2-003 · MW05 · 2026-05-13
Reported hardness
412 mg/L as CaCO₃
How
Reported by the laboratory, not derived
Method
APHA 2340C — EDTA titration
Reporting limit
1 mg/L

Cross-checked against the major cations

InputValue
Calcium (filtered)96.4 mg/L
Magnesium (filtered)41.2 mg/L
Formula2.497 × Ca + 4.118 × Mg
Computed hardness410.3 mg/L as CaCO₃
Agreement●0.4% against the reported value — within the ±10% reconciliation limit

Reported and computed hardness agree, so the criterion below rests on a number two independent measurements support. Where they disagree by more than 10% the result is a review item, because the criterion inherits the error.

The relationship, and where it stops

criterion = base × (hardness ÷ 30) ^ slope, evaluated at the capped hardness of 400 mg/L as CaCO₃

Capped. Capped at 400 mg/L. ANZG does not extrapolate the hardness relationship above that, so the criterion is computed at the cap rather than at 412 — the conservative direction, and it is stated rather than silently applied.

What the cap costs, stated rather than hidden:

  • Measured hardness412 mg/L
  • Hardness used400 mg/L
  • Zinc criterion at 4128.19 µg/L
  • Zinc criterion at the cap8.00 µg/L
  • Outcomes that change0

The cap makes the criterion slightly stricter, never looser. Extrapolating the relationship past the range it was derived over would be the silent choice, and it would be the one that favours the operator.

Rule version hardness-modified-tv v3 · bound to ANZG 2018 2018.1 — bound to the criteria set, not to the instance.

What it produced, analyte by analyte

Base value, exponent, resulting criterion, and the result it was compared against.
AnalyteBase valueExponentCriterion hereResultOutcomeNote
Cadmium (filtered)0.2 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.890.54 µg/L< 1.0 µg/LindeterminateThe LOR sits above the criterion, so the hardness adjustment does not rescue it.
Nickel (filtered)11 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.8511 µg/L14.2 µg/LexceedanceExceeds at 1.3×.
Zinc (filtered)8.0 µg/L at 30 mg/L0.858.0 µg/L31.6 µg/LexceedanceExceeds at 4.0×, and the batch matrix spike says the true value may be higher.
Why this screen exists

If hardness were 120 mg/L rather than 400, the zinc criterion would be 2.8 µg/L rather than 8.0 and the exceedance factor would be 11× rather than 4.0×. A criterion that moves by a factor of three on another analyte’s result is not a footnote.

So the hardness result is not a supporting analyte on a crosstab. It is an input to three criteria, and it is treated here as what it is — with its own reconciliation, its own cross-check and its own place in the lineage of every value it governs.

Could not be assessed

Results where nothing can be said either way, and what it would take to change that.

This is a finding, and it belongs in the report.

11 results were reported below a limit of reporting that sits above the guideline value — 6 cadmium and 5 PFAS totals. Nothing was measured either way. They are not compliant and they are not exceedances, and writing them into either column is the single most consequential error available here; a support thread on an incumbent records exactly that happening by default.

Two analytes, and only one of them is a purchasing decision.

Cadmium is a reporting limit the laboratory can lower for money, and the panel below prices it. The PFAS totals are not the same problem: the ANZG 2018 guideline value for the sum is 0.13 ng/L and the limit of reporting on the suite is 2.0 ng/L, which is where commercial USEPA 1633 reporting sits. No amount of money moves that this quarter, so the honest answer for those rows is that they stay unassessable and the report says so — which is what this register exists to make possible.

MW11 appears nowhere on this register, and that is stated rather than left to be noticed.

The bore has no row here because it has no result. A result that could not be assessed is still a result — it was reported, it carries a limit of reporting, and a criterion sat above it. A bore that was dipped twice and found dry has none of those, and a row saying the laboratory reported < 1.0 µg/L on a sample nobody collected would be a worse claim than could not be assessed. So this register runs over the 6 locations that returned water, and the crosstab draws the same absence as a column that is present and empty.

Closing it is a purchasing decision, so the screen makes it one

Moving cadmium to ICP-MS/MS at a 0.1 µg/L reporting limit:

  • Results that become assessable6 per round
  • Additional cost per round$108
  • Additional cost per year$432
  • Criterion the new limit sits below0.54 µg/L — by 5.4×
  • Rounds of history this fixes0 — it reaches forward only

Nothing here changes a stored result. A method change from the next round is recorded as a comparability note on the plate, because a reporting limit that steps down mid-series is visible in every figure that spans the change.

What the report says

Generated into §3, and worded so a non-technical reader cannot mistake it for a clean result:

Report §3 — Data quality

Cadmium was reported by the laboratory at a limit of reporting of 1.0 µg/L. The applicable ANZG 2018 95% species protection guideline value at the measured hardness is 0.54 µg/L. The reporting limit therefore sits above the guideline value and cadmium could not be assessed against it at any location sampled this round. These results are not reported as compliant. A method offering a limit of reporting of 0.1 µg/L is available and is recommended from 2026 Q3. The same applies to the PFOS + PFHxS sum at 5 locations, where the guideline value of 0.13 ng/L sits below the limit of reporting achievable by USEPA 1633.

Compare the alternative, which is what a product with no state for this produces: 11 rows of 0.001 in a compliance column, and a reader with no way to know.

Only the escalation countdown is scheduled. An exceedance that lands at 09:14 raises its alert at 09:14, inside the same transaction — not on the next tick of a worker that might not run.

Hydrograph

Water level over time, with rainfall, triggers and comparison.

/projects/:projectId/hydrograph

Configuration

Locations · MW05, MW07, MW01A
Period · Jan 2023 – May 2026
Y axis · elevation, m AHD
Rainfall overlay · site gauge, monthly
Trigger line · 195.6 m AHD (TSF licence)
Datum · in force at each measurement date

Saved with the figure, not with the session. QB-3 is that next quarter’s figure is identical except for the new data — which means the configuration is a stored object, not something rebuilt by hand.

A dry bore is a gap. MW11 was dipped to the base of its screened interval on the May round and found dry, so its trace breaks rather than drawing a line through it — and it contributes no point to the potentiometric surface either. A polyline across a null asserts a water level nobody measured.

The same bore, once an hour

Continuous and discrete, drawn apart on purpose

FR-1.10 asks for logger series to be represented separately from discrete results, and the separation is not only a schema decision — a reader has to be able to see which marks somebody stood at the bore for. So the 1,536 hourly water levels are traces and the 3 manual dips are filled marks with a leader, and the plate never averages one into the other.

The dips remain the record. One of them — 2026-04-14 08:05 — is the only water level this bore has for the fortnight the instrument was in the workshop, and another is the one that caught a wrong deployment depth in 999 corrected values. A continuous series is not a reason to stop dipping; it is a reason the dip is worth more.

Same grammar, no new family: closed frame, 1-2-5 ticks, shape and dash for series identity, the second quantity — atmospheric pressure — in its own panel underneath rather than on a second axis. What differs from Figure 4.1 is cadence, and cadence is not a family (§5.8). A Durov or a Schoeller would still need a written grammar proposal before it was drawn.

Why this is a second plate and not a third trace on Figure 4.1

The two plates do not stand on the same baseline, and the difference is metres rather than centimetres. Figure 4.1 draws MW05 at 194.07 m AHD in 2026-05; the round’s own dip at that bore reduces to 199.64 m AHD through the survey in force, and the fitted potentiometric surface holds it at 199.8.

Two of those three agree; the monthly series is the one that does not, and it is the one this plate would have had to join. The finding is recorded rather than fixed in passing, in the seed beside the series it describes, with the six-bore comparison and the reason: re-anchoring changes what Figure 4.1 shows, and it moves this bore from four metres above the licence trigger line to just below it. Which of those is the true relationship between a compliance bore and its trigger is a question with a regulatory answer, and it is not one to settle inside a wave about telemetry.

So the hourly plate is anchored to the field record — the baseline two independent structures corroborate — and drawn beside the monthly one rather than on it. A reader comparing the two elevations is reading a real disagreement, which is why it is said here rather than left to be discovered.

Read it as a table

Every plate has one, and it is not an accessibility afterthought — it is how somebody checks a value they are about to put in a report. A figure a reader has to trust is a figure they will re-derive in Excel.

One finding against the approved grammar, recorded rather than fixed

The rainfall bars are drawn in the rule-strong grey, which measures 2.41:1 against the plate ground — below the 3:1 floor for a mark that carries data. The nearest value that passes is the not-evaluated mark grey at 3.02:1, which is already a token in this product rather than a new colour.

It has not been changed here. The grammar was approved on 20 August and the reference plates are an oracle; a rendering that quietly improves on the thing it is measured against is indistinguishable from a rendering that drifted from it. This is a revision for Jerry to accept or refuse, recorded where it can be seen.

If the revision is accepted:

  • Reference plates to re-render and re-approve3 of 12
  • Contrast against the plate ground2.41 → 3.02
  • Series the bars could now compete with0 — still lighter than every trace
  • Tokens invented0

Not urgent either way. The skill’s own rule is that a contrast warning obliges visible labels or a table view rather than a colour change, and the panel above is that relief. Darkening the bars would be the better fix; leaving them is defensible.

Hydrogeochemistry

Piper, Stiff and Schoeller — what kind of water this is.

/projects/:projectId/hydrochem

What the plate says

Every bore except MW05 is a calcium-bicarbonate water, tightly clustered — the natural signature of the Superficial aquifer here. MW05 is sulfate-dominated and four times the ionic strength.

That is the difference between a bore with a high arsenic result and a bore receiving TSF seepage, and it is the argument a hydrogeologist has to make in the report. The chemistry makes it; the exceedance register alone cannot.

The ions this plate is drawn from balance at MW05 to −0.04% — inside the ± 5% limit, so the shape of the polygon is not an artefact. What does fail is the reconciliation: they sum to 1,698 mg/L against 2,240 mg/L reported, a ratio of 1.32, and a review is raised on it. A plate drawn from data that failed a consistency check should say so on its own face.

Statistics and trend

Censored-data methods and non-parametric trend tests.

/projects/:projectId/statistics

Seasonal Mann–Kendall, on a series that is seasonal

TestSpSen’s slopeVerdict
Mann–Kendall780.0031.77 µg/L per quarter■increasing
Seasonal Mann–Kendall (quarterly blocks)410.0211.52 µg/L per quarter■increasing

The hydrograph on this bore shows textbook wet-season recovery, so the series is seasonal and the plain test treats that structure as trend. Both agree here — the increase is real and survives deseasonalising — but the plain test overstates its significance, and on a shorter series it can manufacture one. Reporting only the plain result on a seasonal series is a defensible-looking answer to the wrong question.

Both are reported. Showing only the one with the smaller p-value would be choosing the answer.

How the two non-detects entered the trend test

Non-detects enter the test as tied values below every detected result, which is what Mann–Kendall’s statistic is built for — it compares ranks, not magnitudes. They are never substituted, and the two here fall below the lowest detection so no tie is ambiguous. Where a non-detect has a limit above a detected value the pair is indeterminate and is scored as a tie rather than guessed.

Never substituted

Half the limit of reporting is the common shortcut and it puts an invented number into a rank test. With an LOR that stepped from 5.0 to 1.0 µg/L mid-series, substitution would have manufactured a step change of 2 µg/L at the method change — a trend created by the laboratory changing instrument.

Why not a linear regression

Environmental series are not normal, are not evenly spaced, and contain values the laboratory reported only as “below something”. Ordinary least squares assumes away all three.

Mann-Kendall asks only whether later values tend to exceed earlier ones, which is the question, and Sen’s slope gives a rate that a single outlier cannot swing.

Below n = 8 the test is reported with a sample-size warning and no p-value, rather than a number that looks like evidence.

Background comparison

Downgradient against reference, and where a site-specific trigger value comes from.

/projects/:projectId/background

At a mine this is the assessment, and a guideline value alone does not make it.

A default guideline value answers “is this water safe”. Background answers “did we cause it”, which is the question a licence condition and a closure argument both turn on. Where no default exists — sulfate has none — background is the only criterion available.

Reference population
MW12 (background) and MW01A, MW03B (upgradient) · 14 quarterly rounds each · 2023-01 to 2026-05
Method
ANZG 2018 §3.1.4 — site-specific trigger value as the 80th percentile of the reference distribution, applied where a default guideline value is absent or demonstrably unrepresentative.
Reference distribution against the downgradient bore, per analyte.
AnalyteBackground median80th percentileDefault guidelineTrigger adoptedMW05VerdictBasis
Sulfate as SO₄112 mg/L148 mg/Lnone — no ANZG DGV148 mg/L918 mg/L6.2× the site-specific triggerDerived — no default exists
Electrical conductivity890 µS/cm1,140 µS/cmLicence ≤ 2500 µS/cm1,140 µS/cm3,410 µS/cm3.0× background, 1.4× the licence limitBoth apply; the licence governs compliance
Arsenic (filtered)2.1 µg/L3.4 µg/LANZG 13 µg/Lnot adopted28.4 µg/L8.4× background, 2.2× the DGVDGV applies — a default exists and is representative
Total hardness128 mg/L166 mg/L—not a criterion412 mg/L2.5× backgroundContext for the hardness-modified values

What the pattern says

Every parameter elevated at MW05 is elevated against background as well as against a guideline, and the signature — sulfate, EC and hardness together — is TSF seepage rather than natural variation. Two bores upgradient in the same unit show none of it.

The signature

Sulfate 6.2×, electrical conductivity 3.0× and hardness 2.5× above background, together, at one bore in a line of seven. Two bores upgradient in the same hydrostratigraphic unit show none of it, and the nested confined bore is at higher head so it is not coming from below.

Any one of those numbers is arguable. The four together, with the flow direction, are not.

See it on the Piper plateFlow direction

Deriving the trigger honestly

The 80th percentile is computed over 42 reference results with two censored, using Kaplan–Meier rather than substitution. A site-specific trigger value derived by substituting half the limit of reporting would sit lower and manufacture exceedances.

Adopting the sulfate trigger at 148 mg/L as a criteria set:

  • Reference results behind it42
  • Censored, carried by Kaplan–Meier2
  • Locations it would apply to4 downgradient
  • New exceedances this round1 — MW05
  • Historical evaluations rewritten0

It becomes a versioned criteria set like any other, with the reference population and the date it was derived recorded on it — so a regulator can see which fourteen rounds of which three bores produced the number, years later.
