One binding. That is the only structural difference between the two cards: same fields, same shape, same everything. There is no external principal type, no guest object and no second code path — an external principal is a principal whose binding list is shorter.

The boundary — and it is the boundary that was already there

The claim this screen is making is a negative one, which is the hardest kind to draw: nothing was built for this. A read by L. Broadbent goes through the same repository layer, narrows through the same single predicate, and lands on the same row-level policy as a read by anybody in the operator’s own team. There is no external branch to get wrong, because there is no external branch.

What it reaches, and by what mechanism

  • The project’s records — locations, samples, results, criteria, exceedances, figures, the draft report — The same repository layer every screen reads through. A read narrows through one predicate and no repository writes a project filter of its own. ●Identical to an internal Contributor
  • The trail of any row it can read — A trail is readable exactly when its subject row is — the read walks back to the row and applies that row’s own scope, so there is no second rule to get wrong. ●Identical to an internal Contributor
  • Every control a Contributor binding carries — import, review, validate, qualify, produce figures — The role decides, not the party. Contributor is one of the closed set of four, and this binding is one of them like any other. ●Identical to an internal Contributor

Three rows and the third column is the same on all three, which is the finding rather than a repetition: there is nothing on this list an internal Contributor reaches differently.

Two mechanisms, and they fail differently on purpose

The primary control is in the application: a read arrives with a scope, narrows through one predicate every repository shares, and a read that arrives with no grant admitting it throws. Underneath, the database policy returns zero rows — because a policy cannot safely raise, and one that did would take the instance down on a missing setting.

The difference is not redundancy. “You do not have access” and “this project has no data” are different sentences and a reader has to be given the right one, so the layer that can raise does, and the layer that cannot fails closed and silent beneath it.

The proof that the seam holds is older than this screen: the catalogue has held two projects since wave 5, and the isolation was measured screen by screen rather than asserted. An engagement adds a shorter binding list to that, not a new axis.

6 things this engagement cannot reach — each with the mechanism that refuses it, because “they cannot see the other project” is a claim and the mechanism is the evidence for it.
What it cannot seeWhat refuses itWhere that surface is
MOCK-KRJ — its bores, its rounds, its one unacknowledged exceedanceThe grant list holds one project. The repository layer throws when a read arrives with no grant that admits it; the policy beneath returns zero rows, because a policy cannot safely raise.The project list
The cross-project registers — the obligations board and the project list, as a portfolioNeither is a special surface. They render what the bindings admit: two rows for the signed-in principal, who holds two; one row for this engagement, which holds one. There is nothing to switch to.The obligations board
Sign-off, issue, and lodging a submissionApprover is not in this binding. A control a binding does not carry is absent rather than present and refusing — which is the rule the project list already states about roles.Approval and sign-off
What any other principal did, across the instanceThat read is not a project scope at all. It needs an auditor binding — the one role that is instance-wide by nature, and the one that cannot be arrived at from a project however many projects a scope holds.The audit trail
The audit table itself, read directlyDenied to the application role outright. The trail is read through a role of its own that holds no project scope, so it cannot be used to read around the walk back to the subject row.The audit trail
The deployment — version, upgrade window, backup drill, entitlement, diagnosticsNot a project binding at all. These surfaces belong to whoever operates the instance, and no role in the closed set of four reaches them by holding a project.Instance health

And one thing the trail cannot answer, said here rather than discovered later.

The audit record is a record of mutations — every write, with its before and after state and the principal who made it. A sign-in is deliberately not audited at all: it is the act that establishes the principal, so there is no principal to attribute it to. So “what did the consultants touch” is answerable and “what did the consultants look at” is not, and no amount of care with this engagement changes that. An operator who needs the second needs something this product does not have.

What v1 does not have, as decisions

Each of these is a thing this screen could have drawn and does not, with the reason it does not. A mockup that draws a form over a table the product has no column for is the most expensive kind of drawing: it looks like specification and it is fiction.

No consultancy identity modela decision, not a gap

What the product actually holds: A role binding is five columns — created_at, directory_group_id, id, project_id, role — and a test asserts that none of them names a principal, a user, a member, a subject or an email. There is nowhere on a binding to put a party, a sponsor or an end date.

So: The engagement record on this screen is what the S8 dimension would add. It is not a description of a table that exists, and this screen says so rather than drawing a form over nothing.

Checked against the role-binding column assertion in the app repo’s provisioning suite.
No cross-client view for the consultanta decision, not a gap

What the product actually holds: Every token’s tenant claim must equal the one tenant this deployment is pinned to, and a multi-tenant authority is refused at configuration, again at discovery, and again on every token.

So: A consultant engaged by three operators signs in to three instances. There is no surface that joins them and building one would be the opposite of what single-tenancy is for — it is the decision, not a missing feature.

Checked against the three tenant-pinning checks in the app repo’s auth layer.
The end date is a record, not yet a policya decision, not a gap

What the product actually holds: A grant carries one field today: the project. A facility subset and the engagement window are named in the code as the two extension points and are deliberately not declared as fields yet, on the stated ground that an unread field rots.

So: So the countdown on this screen is something the sponsor acts on, and what actually ends the access is the directory group emptying. Drawing an enforced expiry would be drawing a policy the product does not have.

Checked against the two named extension points on the grant type.
No user table, and no path to onea decision, not a gap

What the product actually holds: The customer’s directory is the source of truth. Strataflow holds a principal — the subject claim and the claims that came with it — and holds it because an audit record must stay answerable after the person has left.

So: An external person needs an identity in the customer’s directory and membership of the group above. Whether that is a guest invitation, a contractor account or a federation the customer already runs is the customer’s process; Strataflow neither performs it nor records it, and does not create, name or manage the group either.

Checked against the glossary’s principal and directory-group entries.

A consultant on three operators’ sites signs in three times

That is not an oversight in the drawing and it is not a roadmap item. One deployment per customer, in the customer’s own cloud, pinned to one directory tenant — and the pinning is checked three times over, because the failure mode is silent: point the instance at a multi-tenant authority and every standard check still passes while it quietly accepts sign-ins from every tenant there is.

So the consultancy has three identities in three directories and three sets of bookmarks, and there is no surface anywhere that shows them one list of their work. Building that surface would mean joining data across customers, which is the one thing this architecture exists to make impossible. The inconvenience is the guarantee, seen from the other side.

The operator gets the other half of the same trade: nothing about this engagement is visible to, routed through, or dependent on the vendor. There is no external-party directory Strataflow keeps, because there is no Strataflow-operated anything.

Where it would live, which is the whole test

The requirement on this dimension has never been “build it”. It has been that the information architecture must accommodate it later without route restructuring — a test on the architecture, run now, rather than a licence to draw the feature.

This recordWould be
The engagement/instance/access/engagements/:engagementId
Its parent/instance/access — a route that already exists
The project-side viewthe project home — a panel on a page that already exists
Routes that would move0
New top-level sections0

A binding is already an instance-level record and access is already a section. An engagement is a record about a binding, so it is a child of the screen that lists them — and the project manager’s view of it is a panel where they already look for who else is in here. Nothing above either one moves.

And this catalogue’s own brief says that test is not a licence to draw the feature, which is why what is drawn is the seam and the decisions rather than the thing itself. There is no form here that creates an engagement, no directory these controls reach, and no screen anywhere that lists a party the operator has not contracted with. The one thing a drawing can settle — does the architecture have room for this — is settled above.

The authorisation model passes the same test on its own terms: a scope is a set of grants rather than a list of project ids, precisely so this dimension is a field on a grant and a clause in one predicate rather than a rewrite of every query. The anchors already carry a facility column that nothing reads yet, kept so the site-subset half has somewhere to land.

How the access ends, and what outlives it

Four things happen when it ends, and three of them are “nothing”

  1. 1The group is emptied, or deletedIn the customer’s directory, by the administrators who already run joiners and leavers. Nothing is done in Strataflow, and there is nothing in Strataflow to forget to do.
  2. 2The next request refusesMembership is resolved from the directory on every request rather than read from the token, so nothing waits for a session to expire and nobody keeps working for the rest of the day.
  3. 3The work stays with the operatorEvery result validated, every qualifier applied, every figure and every draft section stays. Withdrawing access and erasing history are different acts, and only one of them was asked for.
  4. 4The trail stays answerable, permanentlyEvery row they wrote still carries their principal. “Who validated this” is answerable in five years by someone who has never heard of the consultancy, which is the whole reason attribution is at the database rather than in the application.

None of it has happened — the four stages are drawn waiting, because the engagement has 26 days left. It ends the way the contract ends, and what the operator keeps is what the contract said they keep: the work products stay with them, which is the requirement this dimension has carried since it was written down.

And the honest part: nothing enforces the date

The countdown above is a record with a clock beside it. What actually ends the access is somebody emptying SG-Strataflow-WDL-Ext-Coolibah in the directory — and if nobody does, L. Broadbent keeps a working Contributor binding on 2026-06-19 and on every day after it.

That is exactly the failure the S8 dimension is written to remove: the engagement window belongs on the grant, so access ends with the contract rather than with somebody remembering to revoke it. It is named in the code as one of two extension points and deliberately left undeclared, on the stated ground that an unread field rots.

Ending it now, from this screen — what that would write:

  • Directory groups emptied1
  • Principals refused at their next request2
  • Rows deleted0
  • Results, qualifiers and draft sections withdrawn0
  • Audit rows re-attributed or removed0

Reversible in the only sense that matters: re-adding the group restores the reach, and nothing was destroyed to remove it. What cannot be undone is that the engagement ended on a date, which is a fact and stays on the record.

The control is drawn against a directory this catalogue does not have. It is here because a screen that shows an expiry and offers no way to act on it teaches the reader to go and do the real work somewhere else — which is how an expiry date becomes decoration.

What they have touched — 1 recorded act

The same six columns as every other row on the trail, because it is the same trail.
AtPrincipalActionTableWhat
2026-05-22 11:31:06lbroadbent@coolibah.exampleupdatelocationMW07 · area corrected from Borefield to TSF

A bore filed under the wrong area is a real defensibility problem — every area summary in the report counts it in the wrong place — and it is exactly the kind of thing a hydrogeologist reading a network for the first time finds. It is recorded here as L. Broadbent’s act, by the database, with no application code deciding to record it.

The whole trail, and how to ask this question of it

There is no “external” column on an audit row, and adding one would be a mistake.

What makes this act findable is the subject it already carries. The party owns that domain, the operator’s directory issued the identity, and the trail records what the request arrived as — so the answer to “what did the consultants touch” comes out of the data rather than out of a flag somebody has to remember to set. A flag would be a second copy of a fact the directory owns, and a second copy is a thing that drifts.

The drill runs the whole cycle — back up, write more, drop the database, restore, measure. An untested restore is not a backup.

Customer-initiated diagnostics

There is no telemetry from a customer deployment, so a diagnostic bundle is something the customer runs and sends: version, configuration, logs, schema state, recent errors.

In the bundleNot in the bundle
Version and commitAny monitoring result
Migration stateAny location or coordinate
Recent errors, redactedAny principal identifier
Schema and policy inventoryAny certificate or report

Restore is not done until the content check passes.

The backup writes a manifest — audit and lineage digests, the trigger, policy and grant inventory — and the restore is measured against it. A database that comes back up with its audit triggers missing has restored the data and lost the record.

Four states, everywhere

Empty, loading, partial and error — designed once, for every surface.

/help/states

Three rules the words have to keep, and they are the reason this is a screen rather than a component.

No empty headline may read “No data”. An empty queue and an empty register are different sentences — you are finished against nothing has arrived — and a screen that confuses them tells a practitioner their work is done when it has not started. Every partial state must quantify what is absent, because “some data” is exactly when a number is needed most.

Empty — and the two kinds of empty

An empty queue — you are finished

The reward state. It says what was checked and when, so it is a claim rather than an absence.

○ Nothing needs you.

Every exception is dispositioned and no obligation is inside its warning window. Last checked 2026-08-23 07:41 AWST.

An empty register — nothing has arrived

The onboarding state, and the first thing a new customer sees. It teaches the first action.

○ No results on this project yet.

Results arrive by importing a laboratory deliverable. Nine locations are registered and the 2026 Q3 round is planned, so everything is ready for the first file — drop it on the import screen and the format is named before anything is read.

Loading — and it must not shift when the data lands

The skeleton reserves the real grid

Seven columns because the crosstab fills seven, at the row height it will use. A grid that jumps after four seconds reads as broken even when it is correct.

Reading 2,841 results…

Evaluating against 2 criteria sets. On a site link this takes about 9 seconds.

A long operation says how long

Anything that can exceed about a second shows determinate progress. An indeterminate spinner cannot be told from a dead connection.

Evaluating 2,841 results against 2 criteria sets68%

1,932 of 2,841 · about 4 seconds left · you can leave this page and it continues

PAS2026-04417_Wandalup_2026Q2.zip · 38 MB23%

8.7 MB of 38 MB · 41 KB/s · about 12 minutes left

Interrupted transfers resume from where they stopped. Closing this tab does not lose the upload.

Partial — quantify what is missing

Some of it is here

The count is the whole point. “Some data” is not a state a practitioner can act on.

◐ 53 of 63 planned results are in. 3 of them are held in quarantine and 10 were never collected.

MW11 was not sampled in the 2026 Q2 window, which closed 2026-05-14 in Australia/Perth: the bore was dipped twice and found dry. The crosstab stays complete for every other location and this one’s column is drawn empty rather than omitted — a missing column reads as a bore that does not exist, and a blank cell reads as a value somebody forgot to enter. It carries the round’s own dry disposition — glyph and word — and the reason, across all 11 of its cells.

The statistics know they are partial

A summary computed over an incomplete round is not wrong, but it is not the round either, and the difference belongs on the surface that shows it.

◐ This median is over 6 of 7 locations.

MW11 has no 2026 Q2 result — dry, not missed. The estimator is Kaplan–Meier over the round’s 66 results of which 14 are censored; a bore that returns to water next quarter changes it, and the figure carries the same note in its provenance strip so a copy pasted into Word does not lose the caveat.

Error — say what happened and what to do

A not-found is not “something went wrong”

And it deliberately cannot be told apart from a refusal, because saying “this exists but you may not see it” is itself a disclosure.

▲ There is no project at this address, or you do not have access to it.

Both read the same on purpose — telling you which one it is would confirm the existence of something you are not entitled to see. If you expected access, your administrator adds you to the project’s directory group.

A session that lapsed mid-form loses nothing

This is the field officer on a phone whose session expired between filling the form and pressing the button. The old behaviour was a bare “Something went wrong / 401”.

▲ Your session expired while this page was open.

The nine readings you typed are held on this device and have not been sent. Signing in again returns you to this form with every value still in it — nothing needs retyping and nothing was written twice.

Two more states that are not on anybody’s list

⇄ D. Okafor changed this at 2026-08-23 07:38 AWST, while you were editing.

The validation state of this result moved from screened to validated. Your change has not been written and nothing has been lost.

Now on the recordvalidated
Yours, unsavedrejected

▲ The stats worker did not answer, so the trend is absent rather than wrong.

Mann–Kendall and Sen’s slope are computed by a separate service and it is unreachable. Everything on this page that does not depend on it is correct and current; the trend column is empty and labelled, not filled with a stale number from the last time it worked.

Keyboard and assistance

The contract for somebody who works here every day, and the help for somebody who does not.

/help/keyboard

A two-hundred-question review queue is a session, not an afternoon — and that is a keyboard claim.

Every queue and grid a practitioner works daily is fully operable without a mouse. This is not an accessibility afterthought bolted to a mouse-first design; it is the difference between a tool somebody is fast in and a tool somebody endures.

The palette, and why it is not a search box

Search finds things. The palette runs verbs, and it is the fastest path to a screen a practitioner visits monthly and cannot remember the location of.

  • Actions
  • Go to
↑↓ move↵ runesc close

Destructive verbs appear in the palette and never execute from it — “Reverse a committed import…” opens the reversal screen with its blast radius, because a keystroke that withdraws 231 results is not a shortcut, it is a trap.

Assistance that is not a help centre

A term, defined where it is used

The vocabulary is bound to the glossary and a guard defends it, but a bound vocabulary a reader has not learned is still jargon. So LOR and indeterminate carry their definitions, and the dotted underline is quiet on purpose. Marking every domain noun would underline half a dense register and teach the reader to ignore all of them.

And the product explains its own decisions in place. The importer applied this without asking because “Sulphate” is an exact synonym in the analyte dictionary — a spelling, not a judgement. It is recorded on each of the 7 results and reverses with the import. sits next to the thing it explains, rather than in a document somebody has to know exists.

Export is assistance too

The commonest reason a practitioner leaves a product is to do one thing it will not do. Export is how they come back.

Exports what is on screen — this filter, these columns, this sort.

Exactly what is on screen: this filter, these columns, this sort. Censored values keep their notation and numbers stay numbers — an export that writes <1.0 into a text column has handed back a spreadsheet that cannot be summed, and one that writes 1.0 has handed back a lie.

The viewer’s own audit — not a product screen

34register surfaces owned

Twenty screens were added in this pass and 17 of them are register surfaces. The other three are J10 — the data states, the keyboard contract and this page — which answer cross-cutting expectations rather than owning a section. Two numbers, two denominators, and they are not the same claim.

Exhaustive relative to six closed lists, and no further.

Absolute exhaustiveness is unfalsifiable. This is complete against the fourteen global expectations, the register’s own section list, the twenty-seven findings of the 22–23 August audit — and, since 1 September, the PRD requirement register, the incumbent capability baseline and the nine journeys of EXPANSION_BRIEF.md §8 — and it has a hole the moment any of those grows. It grew twice on 2 September 2026: the brief’s deferred telemetry journey is walked below as a tenth row, so the journeys table is now measured against ten rather than nine — and the PRD register gained OD-2, which is not a requirement but a resolved open decision from that document’s §14, so its denominator moved by one as well. A list that grows is the honest outcome; a denominator that moves without saying so is not. Four findings are marked n/a rather than claimed: three are properties of a running application that a single static document does not have, and one is a development-server defect with no design content. Marking them covered would have been the easier lie.

A fourth list — what reading the screens as a practitioner turned up

This list had no document behind it, which is what makes it worth keeping.

The three enumerations above came from things this repository already held. These nineteen came from going through the screens as a hydrogeologist and a laboratory data manager would, asking what they would look for and fail to find. Nothing generated the list and nothing defends it — so it is the least trustworthy table on this page, and the most valuable.

AreaWhat was missingScreenWhat it does
DefensibilityField parameter stabilisation and purge recordspurgeThree consecutive readings in tolerance, with the bore that never stabilised recorded as a stated judgement rather than an invisible one.
DefensibilitySample receipt condition and chain of custodyreceiptCooler temperature, seals, preservation and a cracked container — and custody as a chain of transfers rather than a scanned form.
QA/QCThe full QC sample taxonomyqcLaboratory duplicate, method blank, LCS, matrix spike and duplicate, rinsate blank — added to the field and trip blanks already there.
QA/QCThe laboratory batch a QC result coversbatchesA control sample applies to a batch. Without it, a failed spike qualifies everything or nothing.
QA/QCAcceptance limits as versioned configurationqc-limitsWith a source, an effective date, and the applicability rule that was wrong — RPD only above 5 × the reporting limit.
QA/QCData quality assessment against objectivesdqaPrecision, accuracy, representativeness, comparability, completeness, sensitivity — written before the round, not assembled after it.
EvaluationHow a hardness-dependent criterion was calculatedhardnessThe input, its cross-check, the equation, the cap and the three exceedances that rest on it.
EvaluationA register of what could not be assessedindeterminateThe state neither incumbent has, as a finding with a cost to close rather than a footnote.
EvaluationBackground and site-specific trigger derivationbackgroundThe comparison a mine actually makes, and where a site-specific value comes from when no default exists.
EvaluationSeasonal Mann–Kendall, and censored values in the trendstatisticsBoth tests reported on a seasonal series, and how the non-detects entered the rank test.
HydrogeologyPotentiometric surface and flow directionmapA planar fit that derives “downgradient” instead of storing it as a string, with the confined bore excluded.
HydrogeologyThe bore nest, read verticallylocationAn upward gradient from the confined unit is a containment argument, and it is invisible in a register of points.
StatutoryThe Contaminated Sites Act dutynotificationA second clock on the same moment of awareness, to a different branch of the regulator. Discharging one discharges neither.
StatutoryAnnual Audit Compliance ReportobligationsA DWER annual return distinct from the AER, which the board did not carry.
StatutorySubterranean fauna monitoringstygofaunaA WA approval condition assessed on population persistence, and the screen refuses to draw a trend through four points.
ContentPFAS assessed against the operative frameworkcriteriaThe NEMP carries a value per receptor; ANZG alone is insufficient once a potable or recreational receptor is downgradient.
WorkflowThe round on two programmes at onceprogrammeA TARP-escalated monthly programme alongside the quarterly one — the escalated round is the one that gets missed.
WorkflowAssignment and hand-overhomeA thread that hangs off the exceedance rather than off a chat channel, so it is still attached in two years.
LayoutThe results grid across roundscrosstabThe comparison a review is, and the only layout that shows a reporting limit stepping mid-series.

Findings from the August audit — the designed answer to each

The journeys, walked step by step — nine added 1 Sep 2026, the deferred tenth added 2 Sep 2026

A journey is owned when every step lands on a drawn screen that is not a proposal.

Each step below is a link, or a named hole. Written 1 September 2026: “The deferred telemetry journey is not walked: EXPANSION_BRIEF.md defers it with Domain K, matching the PRD’s S8 marking, and walking it would require inventing the screens it defers.” Corrected 2 September 2026: it is walked, and the sentence was right about the cost — walking it did require drawing the two screens it defers, and they are drawn as proposals rather than as product surfaces. The S8 marking on FR-1.10 and FR-3.10 is untouched and both rows above say so. Journey 9 was the one held open by the data rather than by a drawing — a portfolio cannot be drawn honestly from a one-site seed, and the answer was a second project in seed.mjs rather than a screen. It carries 4 bores, 4 rounds and 4 obligations, and its workspace is deliberately not drawn: the walk crosses two projects and then descends into the one this catalogue owns, which is what the note on its row says.

What a green row here does not mean

It means the expectation has been drawn. It does not mean it is built, and it does not mean it is right.

Both design oracles this catalogue is drawn to were self-approved and neither has been printed. A practitioner has now looked at four of these screens — a senior hydrogeologist reviewed the field-capture grid, the QA/QC workspace, the lineage panel and the interpretation editor on 1 September 2026, the four with the most invention in them, and returned four P0 design changes and a binding keep-list. All four are answered here: field capture rebuilt around the bore session, QA/QC around the decision layer, provenance beginning at the bore rather than at the deliverable, and the interpretation editor carrying evidence for the inference rather than for its citations. What that does not mean is that the answers are right — the same practitioner has not seen them, and the redesigned screens now carry more invention than the ones the review corrected, not less.

The lesson of that review is the one worth keeping past it: the drawn version of both screens was internally consistent, carefully argued and wrong on an axis, and no amount of re-reading would have found it. Five minutes of a practitioner’s attention was worth more than the day of drawing that produced them.

A catalogue is easy to make look complete while the judgements inside it are wrong, and this table measures completeness only.

Re-run the three enumerations rather than reading this table. It was assembled by hand and hand-maintained summaries rot, fastest in whichever direction flatters the person writing them.
